question: How are gross margins calculated in the org? At what granularity level is the information available?
reference_answer: Gross Margin % = (Net Revenue - Cost of goods sold) / Net Revenue x 100, where COGS is the landed cost of items sold including inbound freight. It is reported monthly and year to date, split by product category and channel; concession sales are excluded.

question: Customer churn rate - how is that calculated? What dashboards use it?
reference_answer: Churn Rate % = customers in the start base with no purchase for 180 days by quarter end / customers in the start base x 100. The start base is every identified customer with at least one completed order in the 180 days before the quarter starts. It is used on the Customer 360 Dashboard and the Executive KPI Pack. The v1 version is Deprecated.

author: claude
question: What is NRR and how is it different from churn?
reference_answer: NRR (KPI-010) measures how much net revenue is kept from an existing customer cohort over 12 months: current 12-month net revenue from the base cohort / prior 12-month net revenue from the same cohort x 100, excluding new customers. Churn Rate (KPI-007) counts the share of start-base customers with no purchase for 180 days. NRR is revenue-based and can exceed 100%; churn is a customer count.
key_facts: New customers acquired during the period are excluded
review: drafted by Claude, owner to review; two KPIs; NRR is revenue-based, churn counts customers

question: How many days do we use to count an Active Customer?
reference_answer: 30 days. Active Customer (KPI-006) is an identified customer with at least one completed purchase in the last 30 days, and the 30-day window is the only certified definition. The 90-day figure in the Customer Team FAQ is informal and has no standing; informal definitions that conflict with a Certified KPI do not apply (POL-01).

question: What is the difference between Active User and Active Customer?
reference_answer: Active Customer (KPI-006, Certified) needs at least one completed purchase in any channel in the last 30 days. Active User (KPI-020, Provisional) is a logged-in app user with at least one session in the last 30 days; no purchase is needed. They are different KPIs and must not be mixed.

question: How is DSO calculated and which customers does it cover?
reference_answer: DSO = (accounts receivable at period end / credit sales in the period) x number of days in the period. It covers credit sales to wholesale partners and corporate gifting clients; retail sales paid at checkout are out of scope.

wholesale partners and corporate gifting clients

author: claude
question: What did the old churn rate (v1) measure and why was it replaced?
reference_answer: Churn v1 (KPI-007-V1) was the share of loyalty members who close their loyalty account in a month. It was replaced because most customers who stop buying never close their account, so it understated churn, and customers without a loyalty account were invisible. It is Deprecated and replaced by KPI-007 v2 (180 days without a purchase) from 2026-04-01; it must not be used for reporting.

author: claude
question: How does a KPI go from Provisional to Certified?
reference_answer: The KPI owner submits the definition (it starts as Provisional, version below 1.0). The data steward checks that sources and dashboards are in the data catalog and runs a two-month parallel test that must reconcile within 1% against an independent calculation. The owner presents to the monthly KPI Council; if approved the version becomes 1.0 and the status Certified, and the glossary is updated within 5 working days. Certified KPIs are reviewed every 12 months.
review: drafted by Claude, owner to review; two-month parallel test, KPI Council approval
